html:
Indian indenture was a system of contract labour under which over a million Indians were shipped to work on plantations in British and other colonies between 1834 and 1917.

It began after Britain's abolition of slavery left sugar planters short of workers. Mauritius received the first ships in 1834. Recruits, mostly poor villagers from Bihar, eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Tamil country, signed contracts, usually for five years, often without knowing where they were going. Many were tricked. Wages were low, punishments harsh and death rates on ships and estates high. Critics called it a new system of slavery.

The main destinations were:

  • Mauritius and Réunion.
  • The Caribbean, above all British Guiana and Trinidad.
  • Fiji in the Pacific.
  • Natal in South Africa, and East Africa.

Most never went home. Their descendants make up large shares of the people of Mauritius, Guyana, Trinidad, Suriname and Fiji. Gandhi in South Africa took up their cause, and Indian nationalists made the system's end a demand; recruitment stopped in 1917. Similar flows went to Ceylon and Malaya, such as the Tamil workers to Ceylon estates.
sum: Indian indenture was a system of contract labour under which over a million Indians were shipped to work on plantations in British and other colonies between 1834 and 1917.
